how: Members repeatedly call for building, repairing, and defending several figures rather than gathering around only one mark.
Judgements of capacity concern particular figures and tasks, including the stated need for ten live workers to repair Frisk.
People begin particular figures and name their locations while inviting others to participate.
Starting and recruiting can occur in one utterance, so the record need not expose a separate starter stage before calls.
Calls accompany reported construction, but an uncoordinated figure can enter organised defense without an observed call that produced it.

statement: adopting an uncoordinated figure into organised defense
how: A figure reportedly made without subreddit or chat coordination receives a direct commitment to keep it standing.
Builders report outlines, partial progress, and repeated changes between damaged and repaired states.
Coordinates, grids, and references give dispersed builders usable instructions and a common target.
Private messages seek to bring individual overwriters into the shared plan when public instructions have not reached them.
Members argue over eyes, character identity, and faithful representation while the pictures are already being maintained.
References can coordinate work without resolving design disagreement, as repeated eye reversions and renewed demands for agreement show.
A member updates scripts for blue eyes and receives a direct objection to scripting on community grounds.
Script use and cooldown strain are visible, but no cited passage establishes that exhausted manual defense caused adoption of automation.

statement: relaying plans and agreements between chat and public threads
how: Coordination crosses public threads, chat, and direct messages, with agreements relayed outward and reported design ideas returning as canvas changes.
One room cannot test the cross-room prevalence claim, and visible informal coordination does not establish the absence of decided order in unseen discussions.
A short promise to keep helping contributes a bare commitment without requesting a return.
Bare commitments occur, but the concepts do not establish the proposed preference structure or the frequency of acceptance after recruitment.
Participants keep figures through guarding, repair, border protection, and resistance to announced attacks.
A celebratory completion post is followed by an explicit report that the completed figure still needs maintenance.
Completion may be declared after accepting an imperfection rather than resolving every repair or design dispute.
A deliberate relocation is explained to observers so they will not misidentify the builders as vandals.
Participants propose borders and truces, report agreements, and challenge failures to honour them.
Speakers explicitly claim ambassador or representative roles when carrying proposals between groups.
Participants spare neighboring art, avoid retaliation, and reject expansion that would destroy established work.
A settled treaty is one possible basis for restraint, while respect for existing art can independently limit construction.
Members offer pixels for shared safety and exchange previously defended space as repayment.
A participant explicitly describes an alliance in which each side protects the other side's work.
Border requests may address adjacent space prospectively, so erosion of placed work is not established as the cause of every negotiation.
Help can address shared exposure or repay earlier defense, without demonstrating that the requesting room first exhausted its own hands.
A promise not to expand into a neighbour's work receives a direct offer of spare turns to help preserve order.
The call to stop attacks and fight a shared threat supplies the expressed logic of the later mutual-protection alliance.
Participants carry an agreement into chat and message individual placers, making dissemination a practical task beyond announcing a treaty.
Fractured communication and an unhonoured agreement do not establish an explicit dispute over an envoy's authority to bind placers.
Negotiation receives a reply about fractured communication, but the proposed transition into a dispute over representation is not demonstrated.
Permission to place on another group's space is locally visible through requests, reported refusal, and thanks for allowing the figure.
Reported host permission or refusal supports a partial guest relation without directly observing the host's deliberations or enforceable control over placers.
Destroyed or failed figures prompt explicit replacement builds at newly named locations.
A judgement that destruction is too fast can receive encouragement to stay with the same build rather than a move.

statement: redirecting effort among existing works after a loss
how: A failed project can release effort to maintaining an existing figure rather than rebuilding or ending participation.
Movement proposals can anticipate an approaching neighboring work before the threatened figure has been erased or overrun.
A proposed exchange does not establish an agreed reciprocal outcome when its proponent later reports taking the land anyway.
Participants render canvas events through familiar game lore and jokes without requiring that lore to select a rival.
The cited attacks do not identify an old quarrel carried onto the canvas.
Game language in an attack call does not establish a prior tie that names an external rival and motivates that attack.
Fake announcements, admitted deception, and collaborative joke rewriting operate beside canvas building.
April Fools play includes both separate pranks and jokes made directly from canvas events, so theme membership cannot determine the distinction.
Members question the canvas flood and moderators make a coordination thread prominent while ordinary posters describe displaced attention.
Stickying and objections to the flood support local boundary work without demonstrating a rule that concentrates all canvas posts in one venue.
Returning to ordinary activity includes resubmitting art and comics pushed off the front page by the event.
Participants celebrate completion, credit defenders, and describe what collective work meant to them.
Marking completion can follow accepting an imperfect figure rather than achieving a fully settled design.
Closure announcements, damage accounts, and a timelapse preserve the event and invite recollection of recurring changes.
Celebration and recording are observed, but their sequence alone does not demonstrate that marking the work caused members to preserve its record.
A member challenges the supposed final image by identifying unfinished features and less progress than the remembered endpoint.
A snapshot correction is supported, while valuing damage as battle scars does not establish a dispute over cleaning a shared copy.
A request to explain an alliance story's relevance receives a mutual-protection account and then explicit acceptance of that explanation.
Members continue figure-building on a successor canvas and discuss keeping a partly completed version instead of relocating it.
Successor activity is observed, but no cited passage makes the earlier recording of the canvas its cause or establishes the later build's completion.
Local calls propose destroying another work or attacking an Undertale figure, without proving the proposed placements occurred.
Incoming threats and a visiting group's takeover report must retain their actors rather than count as aggression by the host room.
Participants answer a hostile threat with a survival claim and use a chant against a named attacker.
The coexistence of recruitment and aggression does not establish that a recruitment call caused the later attack calls or incoming threats.
An attack proposal receives a direct challenge framed as April Fools, without an articulated norm or cost explaining refusal.
No cited transition connects the local attack calls to subsequent border negotiation or invocation of a truce.
An explicit threat receives a direct answer claiming the threatened figure is still standing.
